scope: src/main.js lines 12948-14260 — procedural sfx/music/reverb (sfxShoot, sfxDryFire, MUSIC/_scheduleBeat/musicTick, REVERB), close-combat impact feedback (_pulseCloseCombatFeedback, _setCloseCombatHitFlags), and the knife-pair choreography subsystem (_knifePairPhaseDirector/_knifePairTensionEnvelope/_knifePairChoreographySnapshot/_beginKnifePair/_updateKnifePairRuntime/_updateKnifePairContactRig/_finishKnifePair). Cross-checked callers and globals (PP@15615, damp@15140, getAC@audio.js:11, G.building usage, prev-pulse reads at 14687-14689 / 42023 / 43071, music callers at 35366/35455).

findings.title: MUSIC_PROFILES has only 8 entries but the game has 12 buildings; reverb has 12 — late buildings get the wrong music key/tempo
findings.description: MUSIC_PROFILES (line 13071) defines per-building tempo/scale/key for buildings 1-8 only. reverbSetBuilding's profiles array (line 13103) defines 12 entries (adds border crossing, cathedral, karelia freighter, spire). musicSetBuilding clamps with Math.min(bn-1, MUSIC_PROFILES.length-1), so buildings 9-12 silently reuse building 8's 'A-minor blues' @140bpm 'server farm' music while their reverb correctly switches to cathedral/tunnel/etc. The adaptive-score feature is half-wired: it stops scaling per-building exactly where the reverb keeps going. A player reaching buildings 9-12 hears the wrong, mismatched score (fast blues over a cathedral reverb wash).
findings.fix: Add 4 more entries to MUSIC_PROFILES (indices 8-11) matching the 4 extra reverb environments — e.g. {tempo:100,scale:[0,2,3,5,7],rootHz:100,name:'border-crossing'},{tempo:66,scale:[0,2,3,5,7,8,11],rootHz:84,name:'cathedral-harmonic'},{tempo:112,scale:[0,1,5,7,8],rootHz:92,name:'freighter-phrygian'},{tempo:134,scale:[0,3,5,6,7,10],rootHz:98,name:'spire-blues'}. No structural change needed; musicSetBuilding's clamp keeps working.
findings.risk: Pure data addition, no save-state or build impact. Worst case is a subjectively wrong key choice for buildings 9-12 (still strictly better than reusing building 8). Keep array a plain literal so the static probes stay green.

findings.title: _pulseCloseCombatFeedback writes P._knifeThrowImpactPulse for the 'knife_throw' branch, but nothing ever reads it — knife-throw hit feedback is computed and discarded
findings.description: In _pulseCloseCombatFeedback, the kind==='knife_throw' branch is the only writer of P._knifeThrowImpactPulse (verified by grep across all of src/: exactly one reference, the write). Every sibling pulse (_knifeImpactPulse, _knifeStabPulse, _meleeWhipImpact) is read elsewhere to drive viewmodel/camera, but _knifeThrowImpactPulse is never sampled or decayed. The knife-throw close-impact pulse intended to kick the camera/viewmodel on a thrown-knife landing is effectively a no-op — the throw lands with no extra felt feedback even though the code thinks it applied some.
findings.fix: Either (a) consume it: in the viewmodel/camera tick that already reads _knifeImpactPulse, add a small contribution from P._knifeThrowImpactPulse and decay it with damp(...,0,...,dt) like the others; or (b) if no throw-specific feel is wanted, delete the line and rely on the shakeX/shakeY/dmgPitch already applied above it. The shake/pitch still apply, so impact is low.
findings.risk: Option (a) adds a new visible kick on thrown-knife hits (intended) — keep magnitude small to avoid over-shake. Option (b) is zero-risk cleanup. No save/build impact either way.

findings.title: P._knifePairTensionPulse is recomputed and damped every cinematic frame but is never read — wasted per-frame work
findings.description: _updateKnifePairRuntime computes P._knifePairTensionPulse via a clamp over tension.wristLock/counterForce/bladeScrape and runs it through damp() every frame while the knife-pair cinematic is active. Grep across all of src/ shows this is the only reference: it is written and decayed but never sampled by camera, viewmodel, HUD, or enemy logic. It is computed-then-discarded state — harmless but pure dead work each frame of the takedown.
findings.fix: Either delete line 14251 (zero behavioral change) or wire it into the camera/viewmodel — e.g. add a subtle handheld micro-shake while the blade is locked: in the pair camera block (~14237-14239) add a tiny side*tensionPulse*.004 jitter to cameraRoll. Wiring it would make the 'struggle' visibly read on screen, which is on-theme for this subsystem.
findings.risk: Deletion is zero-risk. Wiring it in must use a very small coefficient or it competes with the existing impact/rip pulse camera kicks during the most camera-busy moment.

findings.title: P._knifePairGrabPulse is set on the 'grab' beat and decayed each frame, but unlike sibling slice/impact/rip pulses it is never consumed for camera or viewmodel
findings.description: _triggerKnifePairBeat sets P._knifePairGrabPulse=1 on the grab beat (line 13852) and _updateKnifePairRuntime decays it (line 14247). Its siblings P._knifePairSlicePulse/_knifePairImpactPulse/_knifePairRipPulse are all both set AND read at lines 14233-14235 (camera) and 14687-14689 (viewmodel). Grep shows _knifePairGrabPulse has only the write (13852) and the damp (14247) — no reader. The grab moment of the takedown therefore gets no dedicated camera/viewmodel pulse even though the code allocates and decays state for it; the grab reads weaker than intended.
findings.fix: Mirror the slice pulse: where camera reads slicePulse (line 14234) and where the viewmodel reads slice (line 14688), add a small read of P._knifePairGrabPulse to add a brief inward camera dip / viewmodel anticipation on the grab. Keep coefficient ~half of slice's since grab is pre-impact.
findings.risk: Low — adds a felt beat at the start of the takedown. Use small magnitude so it doesn't fight the bigger impact pulse milliseconds later. No save/build impact.

findings.title: pair.strikeHand / pair.bladeTip are written every frame but never read; only the prev* copies are used
findings.description: _updateKnifePairContactRig writes four Vector3 clones at end of frame: pair.strikeHand, pair.bladeTip (14100-14101) and pair.prevStrikeHand, pair.prevBladeTip (14102-14103). Only the prev* pair is read (the one-frame-lag motion-blur ghost at lines 13957-13962). Grep confirms pair.strikeHand and pair.bladeTip have no readers. Lines 14100-14101 are two extra Vector3 allocations per cinematic frame for no effect — minor GC churn during the takedown.
findings.evidence:
pair.strikeHand=strikeHand.clone();   // line 14100 — no reader
pair.bladeTip=bladeTip.clone();        // line 14101 — no reader
pair.prevStrikeHand=strikeHand.clone();// line 14102 — read at 13958/13960 next frame
pair.prevBladeTip=bladeTip.clone();    // line 14103 — read at 13958/13961 next frame
findings.fix: Delete lines 14100-14101. The prev* assignments (14102-14103) are the ones actually feeding the ghost trail and must stay. Saves two Vector3 allocations/frame during takedowns.
findings.risk: Zero behavioral risk if only 14100-14101 are removed and nothing later in the same frame relies on them (confirmed none do). Build/save unaffected.

findings.title: All SFX connect raw to ctx.destination with no master limiter — heavy auto-fire clips/distorts; a single DynamicsCompressor is a cheap AAA audio polish
findings.description: sfxShoot stacks main crack (gain .55) + slap-back delay (.25) + low thump (.30) + HF crackle (.18) per shot, all connected directly to c.destination (no shared bus). With an auto weapon that is several overlapping shots, plus the music master, all summing into the hardware output un-limited. There is no DynamicsCompressorNode anywhere in src (grep: 0 hits) and 104 direct c.destination connections in main.js alone. During intense combat the output clips, producing audible crackle/distortion that immediately reads as 'amateur audio'. A single shared limiter on the output is the classic one-node fix that makes the whole mix feel produced.
findings.evidence:
s.connect(f);f.connect(g);g.connect(c.destination);s.start();  // line 12966
... dly.connect(g2);g2.connect(c.destination);  // 12976
... lo.connect(lg);lg.connect(c.destination);  // 12988
... cg... cg.connect(c.destination);  // 12997 — four sources per shot, no limiter; grep createDynamicsCompressor => 0
findings.fix: Minimal-touch route: in audio.js getAC(), create the context AND a shared limiter once: AC=new AudioContext(); const comp=AC.createDynamicsCompressor(); comp.threshold.value=-8; comp.ratio.value=12; comp.attack.value=0.002; comp.release.value=0.18; comp.connect(AC.destination); AC._masterBus=comp; return AC. Then expose AC._masterBus and have the hot, layered emitters (at minimum sfxShoot's four .connect(c.destination) at 12966/12976/12988/12997, plus REVERB.dryGain/REVERB.conv in musicInit at 13134-13135) connect to c._masterBus instead of c.destination. Even routing ONLY sfxShoot's four nodes through the limiter audibly tames combat clipping with near-zero risk.
findings.risk: Adding a compressor on the existing summed output can never break audio (it only sums + limits). Routing only the loudest/most-frequent emitter (sfxShoot) keeps the diff tiny and the static probes green. Do not move all 104 destination connects at once — surgical subset is enough and lower-risk.

findings.title: Per-building convolution reverb is wired ONLY to the music master; gunshots/melee never get the room reverb, so every environment sounds acoustically identical
findings.description: musicInit builds a per-building convolution reverb (REVERB.conv / sendGain / dryGain) and reverbSetBuilding swaps a hand-authored IR per environment (dock metallic .55s, subway tunnel 3.2s, cathedral 3.6s, etc.). But the reverb send is fed only by MUSIC.masterGain (lines 13131-13132). Every SFX one-shot — including the loudest, most-heard sound, the gunshot — connects directly to c.destination and bypasses the convolver entirely. The result: a shot in the dock sounds exactly like a shot in the cathedral. The single most impactful 'this place sounds real' AAA cue (gunshot tail length changing per room) is computed (the IRs are built and switched) but never applied to weapons — an effect-built-but-not-wired.
findings.fix: Expose the reverb send (e.g. window-less module ref REVERB.sendGain) and add a parallel tap from the loud impact SFX: in sfxShoot after building g, add a wet send 'if(REVERB.sendGain){const wg=c.createGain();wg.gain.value=cfg.gain*0.35; g... wg... g connects to both c.destination and wg; wg.connect(REVERB.sendGain);}'. Cheapest version: feed only the main crack node (line 12966) into REVERB.sendGain at ~0.3 gain. Guard with if(REVERB.sendGain&&REVERB.conv.buffer) so it no-ops before musicInit.
findings.risk: Reverb is additive and gated by sendGain wet level — worst case is too-wet shots in long-IR rooms (subway/cathedral); start with a low send (~0.25-0.35) and per-weapon scaling. Must null-check REVERB.sendGain because sfxShoot can fire before musicInit. Keep the change inside sfxShoot to limit blast radius and keep probes green.

findings.title: getAC() lazily constructs an AudioContext but no code ever calls ctx.resume(); if the context is created outside a user gesture (or auto-suspended) all sfx/music are silent
findings.description: getAC() returns AC || (AC = new AudioContext()) and never resumes it. Grep across src shows zero .resume() calls on the audio context. Today this usually works because musicInit() (the first audio touch on the main flow) is called right after tryLock() inside click/pointerlock gesture handlers (e.g. lines 32583/32860/35893), so creation lands inside a user gesture and the context starts 'running'. But it is fragile: any code path that triggers a SFX before that gesture (or a browser that creates the context suspended even within the gesture, e.g. iOS Safari), leaves AC in 'suspended' state forever — the entire procedural soundtrack and all sfx are silent with no error.
findings.fix: Make getAC resilient: 'export function getAC(){ if(!AC) AC=new AudioContext(); if(AC.state==='suspended') AC.resume(); return AC; }'. Also call getAC().resume() once inside tryLock()/pointerlock handlers as a belt-and-suspenders gesture unlock. This is idempotent and cannot regress the currently-working desktop path.
findings.risk: resume() returns a promise that can be ignored; calling it when already running is a no-op. Zero save/build impact. Confidence is medium-low only because the current desktop gesture timing already makes it work in practice — the fix is hardening, not a guaranteed live bug.
